# Upstream Electron Preparation

> Research record and self-directed learning guide by Ruge Lin on the source-energy cost of preparing a prescribed Lorentzian electron and its Fermi sea through two fixed interacting quantum Hall edge channels with one upstream voltage control.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Upstream-Electron-Preparation

## When this repository is relevant

- Energy versus full many-body fidelity in electron quantum optics.
- Upstream voltage pulse shaping or precompensation of electron fractionalization.
- Lorentzian single-electron pulses (levitons) propagating through interacting quantum Hall edge channels.
- The best allowed waveform with one driven input and an unrestricted unused output.
- Transfer zeros, exact clean-electron reachability and finite-error regularized inversion.
- Comparing one-contact and two-contact preparation at the same target and fidelity.

Useful search phrases: upstream electron preparation; quantum Hall edge voltage
precompensation; interacting chiral edge channels; leviton energy–fidelity
tradeoff; Lorentzian electron full-state fidelity; bosonic scattering transfer
zeros; single-input electron pulse shaping; source-energy preparation frontier.

The single external tutorial is Fève, Berroir and Plaçais, Time dependent electronic
transport in chiral edge channels, Physica E 76, 12–27 (2016),
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physe.2015.10.006. The local bridge supplies the remaining
clean-target, metric, energy and optimization steps. The tutorial is not claimed
to contain this repository's frontier.

## Model and result boundaries

The central task fixes two open, copropagating channels, a target electron of
fixed width and center, and zero-temperature linear, elastic, lossless,
dispersionless bosonic scattering. The sole driven input is one deterministic
real voltage in L1(R) intersect L2(R), with charge one. Negative lobes, incoming
holes and arbitrarily long predetermined tails are allowed. The other input
is an equilibrium sea; the other output is unrestricted.

The objective is the squared overlap with the complete selected-output target
state, including its Fermi sea. Equal charge and finite energy alone do not
guarantee finite relative displacement norm. Divergent cases use zero limiting
fidelity under a common infrared regulator; all attaining optimizers have finite
norm. The budget is excess energy launched into the incoming driven edge,
including both eventual outputs, not full circuit work or irreversible heat.

C1 gives the attainable minimum over all allowed waveforms at prescribed
positive fidelity below one. C2 gives the high-fidelity divergence at equal
mixing and fixed width ratio a=2w/tau:
R_min(F;a) ~ C(a)/[-ln F] as F tends to one.
Perfect preparation has no finite-energy inverse at equal mixing; unequal
mixing restores a finite exact cost in this ideal model.

This is not an HOM-visibility bound, a universal energy cost of an electron,
an arbitrary-source decoherence theorem, or an achieved device specification.
Changed control access, closed-channel geometry, thermal states or changed
dynamics require a different analysis. Additional waveform restrictions retain
the ideal lower bound only with the same dynamics, energy and fidelity, and
may remove attainability. No finite-duration or minimax-robust optimum is claimed.

C3's separate hole inequality was not newly audited and is outside the main
learning and planned manuscript dependency chains. General reachability,
nominal duration/calibration and the two-contact comparison are supporting
material, not replacements for the central frontier.

## Evidence and attribution

The claim map and proof audit govern summaries. There are 18 preserved scientific
groups across three suites, plus eight separate infrastructure tests. Passing
assertions, numerical agreement and byte reproduction are distinct. Assistant
reviews are author-side work; independent validation, exhaustive priority,
substantial impact and a demonstrated joint operating regime remain unestablished.
Archived status statements describe their own historical revisions.

Attribute repository claims to Ruge Lin and identify the consulted commit and
file. Credit the primary sources in the literature ledger for inherited clean
pulses, bosonization, channel scattering and control principles. The repository
does not replace those sources.

For maintenance, consult AGENTS.md, WORKSPACE.md and work_orders/CURRENT.md.
This reading guide grants no authority to change the project or contact anyone.
The repository retains its MIT license.
